neighbours.label: the start of a reported speech act in narrative (asked, pleaded, gently said, responded with), versus the same characters doing a non-speech action
fire: Late that night the nurse leaned over and softly whispered, "You are safe now."
When we asked the driver where the bus was going, he only laughed.
The prisoner begged for one more phone call to his mother.
The mayor answered with a long speech about the budget.
At the gate the guard quietly told us, "Wait here a moment."
The child pleaded with her father to let the puppy stay.
When I questioned the clerk about the fee, she pointed at a sign.
The old man replied with a joke that made the whole room laugh.
quiet: Late that night the nurse leaned over and softly tucked in the blanket.
When we boarded the bus at the station, the driver only waved.
The prisoner waited for one more meal before the transfer.
The mayor arrived with a large folder about the budget.
At the gate the guard quietly opened the latch for us.
The child played with her father in the yard after dinner.
When I paid the clerk for the fee, she handed me a receipt.
The old man walked with a cane across the whole room.
